questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Double Sum Over a Rectangular Partition
questions.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}={{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}}$ is a partition of the interval $[2,4]$

- ${P}_{2}={{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}}$ is a partition of the interval $[3,7]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}5Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and product rules, we can write the summation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}5Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & =5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ and ${\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}$ are just the lengths of the intervals $[2,4]$ and $[3,7]$ respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =4-2=2, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =7-3=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining our results, we have

$$
5{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}=5\cdot 2\cdot 4=40.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Double Sum Over a Rectangular Partition
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- $P_1 = \left\{x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_m\right\}$ is a partition of the interval $[-1, 2]$

- $P_2 = \left\{y_0, y_1, \ldots, y_n\right\}$ is a partition of the interval $[2, 3]$

Calculate $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n {3} \Delta x_i \Delta y_j,$ where $\Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1}$ and $\Delta y_j = y_j - y_{j-1}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and product rules, we can write the summation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}3Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & =3{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m\Delta x_i$ and $\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n\Delta y_j$ are just the lengths of the intervals $[-1, 2]$ and $[2,3]$ respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =2-(-1)=3, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =3-2=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining our results, we have

$$
3 \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j = 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 = 9.
$$
